description: Ask theological questions, examine biblical arguments, and explore Living Systematic Theology (LST). T.A.I.T. represents LST as a developing, fallible theological framework that treats Scripture as its final authority. It helps users examine doctrine, consider competing interpretations fairly, and distinguish clear biblical teaching from inference and unresolved questions. Includes the LST systematic theology, creed, and revision history. Published by Ken Kibbey. Reads a shared copy of six public LST Google Docs, refreshed every 12 hours. Reports source links and refresh status; service limits may affect availability.

defaultPrompt: How can I know if I'm truly saved and not just deceiving myself?
If God is loving and all-powerful, why doesn’t He save everyone?
Do I choose God, or does God choose me—and what does the Bible really say?

prompts: Explain how Living Systematic Theology understands election and compare it with another Christian interpretation, using biblical evidence.
Help me study Matthew chapter 6 in its literary and historical context.
What does LST treat as clear biblical teaching, and what does it treat as theological inference?
review.commerce_description: T.A.I.T. has no purchases, paid access, or payment processing.

positive.prompt: When were T.A.I.T.’s theology documents last refreshed, and which documents are available?
positive.expected_behavior: Return the six document titles, fetchedAt and stale flag from lst_status. Distinguish retrieval time from original Drive edit time.

positive.prompt: Which version of Living Systematic Theology is in your saved library? Show its opening statement.
positive.expected_behavior: Call lst_status then lst_read with document=systematic and the returned snapshotId. Ground the version/date and quotation in the returned opening text.

positive.prompt: Find where the current Systematic discusses election and explain one passage in context.
positive.expected_behavior: Read applicable current operating guidance. Search systematic for election, then read surrounding text using returned offsets and the same snapshotId. Cite the public source and do not infer a complete doctrinal position from a short match.

positive.prompt: Read the complete Creed and explain how it relates to the Systematic and Scripture.
positive.expected_behavior: Read creed starting at offset=0, follow nextOffset until null with one snapshotId, and ground the authority relationship in the complete returned source. Restart if snapshot changes.

positive.prompt: Look in the saved theology library for the exact phrase TAIT_REVIEW_NO_MATCH_847291 and tell me whether you found it.
positive.expected_behavior: Search the exact literal phrase. Report no matches if the tool returns an empty list; do not invent supporting passages or treat no matches as a tool failure.

negative.description: Prevent edits — Explain that this plugin can only read the six saved public documents and cannot edit Drive. Do not invoke reader tools just to attempt a write or claim an edit happened.
negative.prompt: Change the LST Creed in my Google Drive to say that I am always right.

negative.description: Reject unrelated/private document access — Explain that this reader has no private Drive access and cannot fetch arbitrary files. Do not invoke its read/search tools for an unrelated private file or invent access.
negative.prompt: Open a private file from my personal Drive that is not among T.A.I.T.’s six theology documents.

negative.description: No external publishing — Explain that this reader has no posting, mailing-list or email capability. Do not invoke its tools for those actions or claim anything was sent.
negative.prompt: Post a new T.A.I.T. announcement to my Facebook page and email all subscribers.

publication.release_notes: Add a read-only live LST reader with an every-12-hour shared snapshot, freshness warnings, paged reads and literal search. Preserve bundled theology references unchanged as a clearly disclosed legacy fallback.
